findings.evidence: template/scripts/model_routing.py, `_recover_claude_external_advance`: `for receipt in receipts: if receipt_time <= friction_time: raise RoutingError("the friction event does not predate integration advance receipts...")`. This loops over every receipt in the log with no `opened_at` window. Once any unrelated older receipt exists, recovery is refused for good. design.md Decision 4 and specs/model-routing/spec.md (Scenario "Historical false violation") mention neither this refusal nor the actor-in-delegated-worktree refusal. Only docs/engineering/model-routing.md describes them.
findings.summary: The Claude recovery refusals on receipts are implemented and documented, but the design and spec don't state them. The refusal on any receipt dated at or before the friction event is also unwindowed, so it is broader than the "before receipts existed" wording.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/delegation_containment.py, `_receipt_chain`: `first = next((i for i, r in enumerate(ordered_receipts) if r["before"] == start_head), None); chain = ordered_receipts[first:]`. The comment says earlier in-window receipts are skipped, for example moves that a recovery already accounted for. design.md Decision 2 and the spec's "unbroken receipt chain from the pre-run head" don't describe this tolerance.
findings.summary: The detection-only receipt chain starts at the first receipt whose `before` equals the pre-run head. Windowed receipts that come earlier in time are skipped. design.md Decision 2 says the first `before` must equal the pre-run head.
